newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rebounds broadly as rate nerves ease.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rebounds broadly as rate nerves ease.

text.p: Finnish shares closed around one percent higher on Tuesday to pare recent losses as the market grew confident that a foreseen rate hike in the U.S. would be in line with expectations, brokers said.

The HEX index closed up 0.91 percent at 2,844.90 points as advancing issues beat decliners 57 to 25 with 21 unchanged, and the FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark closed up 1.11 percent at 995.04 after almost reaching 1,000 points.
Volume was a thin 459 million markka with 28.6 percent in telecoms group Nokia.

"We're recovering what we lost," one broker said, adding that the market now discounted the key U.S. federal funds rate to be raised by 25 basis points from 5.25 percent at the Federal Reserve's policy setting FOMC meeting due to end later.
Nokia traded in positive ground all day, but ended just 1.00 markka higher at 301.00 as it was struggling to shake off recent technology stock weakness in the U.S., brokers said.
Cyclicals gained, with metals outperforming and forestries strong on expectations of dollar strength, brokers said.
Forestry group UPM-Kymmene added 1.50 markka to close active 52 million markka trade at 109.30 markka.

Pharmaceuticals group Orion rose on foreign interest after saying on Monday that it had charted good results with a drug that enhanced the effects of conventional Parkinson's disease medications, brokers said.
Orion ended up 7.00 markka at 187.00 in 25 million markka volume, which is hefty for the share.
